notes.title: Can a customer become my employee? Let’s talk about employees in RDS 🔥
notes.content:
[h1]Hey, folks! 👋[/h1]

Welcome back to another development update from your beloved Road Diner Simulator. The last announcement about the cooking in RDS exceeded our expectations when it comes to the engagement which I’m more than grateful for. If you somehow missed it, you can freely catch up by clicking this link as it’s strictly connected to today's one. 

Today, we’re gonna delve deeper into one of the things that give everyone some sleepless nights. Yes, I’m talking about you god damn employees. I’m gonna do my best to give you some details regarding how employees are gonna work in Road Diner Simulator and finally together we’ll try to answer that one tricky question from the title – can a customer become my employee? Are you ready to roll? Grab yourself your favourite drink, cover yourself with a warm blanket, and let’s get right into it 👇

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41182526/46c3b874dd398c0973e1882256a2d773eb19e1d4.jpg[/img]

[h2]How are the employees gonna work in the Road Diner Simulator? 🤔[/h2]

Remember the saying from the previous announcement – It’s not about the cooking – it’s about the stories you uncover? Well that perfectly sums up how you’re gonna be able to hire your employees. But first it’s important to distinguish the difference between a passerby client and a regular one. Let me get straight to the point – passerby is just a money making machine – you won’t be able to build a deeper connection with them. With regular clients that’s a totally different story.

With each all set meal served and each conversation finished, you increase your relationship level with them which uncover their stories, past, and most importantly character. And so we come to this – you’re more likely to remember those regulars (just like in real road diner) hence in a blink of an eye you’ll know what kind of dish they’re most into. Or maybe you want to get some tips regarding running this place? Then, study their behaviour, make sure the meals you serve are top-notch quality, and they might offer something really valuable – knowledge. And as the saying goes – knowledge is power. And the others among regular clients…

[h2]...May become your employees 💥[/h2]

So, to finally answer that question from the title – yes, your customers can become your full time employees. However, it’s not as easy as you might be thinking right now. As mentioned above – first you need to really get to know them to see if they’re fit for a job (for instance one might be great at cooking, and the other might have the necessary knowledge to help you run this place). 

However, being fit for the job is one thing, and character is the other. Some employees might get angry way faster than the others. The others might have some negative perks (imagine the situation when one of your customers is impatiently waiting for the order, but your chef forgot what’s the recipe. That’s rather the recipe for disaster 🥶). And some might demand the payment way faster than the others. Imagine if that would be possible in real life as well…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41182526/c3205b5719c1d176ee0fff7a6ddf7315c0d7a384.gif[/img]

[h2]Stay up-to-date 📰[/h2]

Unfortunately, all good things have to come to an end, future diner owners! I’m really interested to see some of your crazy ideas, suggestions, and what you think about the whole system regarding the employees in Road Diner Simulator. Comment section is yours! Keep those comments coming as we’re constantly analyzing them to see your suggestions!

Now, similarly to the previous devlog, I’d like to know if you have any ideas/topics you want us to delve into? Maybe there is a feature you’re interested in, so make sure to share such information with me in the comments. That’s it from me, and we see each other in the next announcement! 👋

~Sewek

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1747470/Road_Diner_Simulator/

notes.title: The way to every person’s heart is through their stomach – Cooking in RDS 🍳
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41182526/268f7558e7176cd51529150d2470ff699240c921.jpg[/img]

[h1]Hey, folks! 👋[/h1]

It’s that time of the year again, and no – I’m not talking about Christmas (yet). We’re back again with another development update from Road Diner Simulator. We’ve seen dozens of comments from the community whether the game is still in production (of course it is) but I’ll give you some updates regarding that soon! 

Today, we’re gonna delve into cooking in the Road Diner Simulator and basically what you can expect from the game in that matter. As Gordon Ramsay used to say – If you want to become a great chef, you have to work with great chefs, so are you ready to become one? Then, let’s roll! 🔥

[h2]What Road Diner Simulator isn’t 👀[/h2]

Let me get straight to the point – Road Diner Simulator is not a typical Cooking Simulator (which is a great game by the way). It’s not just about running around the kitchen like a headless chicken and paying little to zero attention to your clients – our game delves way deeper than that. Sure, cooking still plays a very crucial role in the game, but it’s not just about cooking – it’s about the stories you uncover. 

[h2]It’s not just about cooking – it’s about the stories you uncover 🍖[/h2]

I’m using this saying not without a reason. The whole idea of cooking in our game is to get to know your clients, set up the foundations and then build stronger connections with them literally through their stomachs. The more time you sacrifice into actually “studying” your clients, the better connections you will be able to build. Some may turn into your regular customers. Others may give you some tips & tricks regarding running your own diner, because they’ve been there before. Some may even help you expand your business. And the others… well who knows – maybe they will turn into your employee one day? 

[h2]What is it gonna look like? 🤔[/h2]

Now, let’s proceed to the more technical side of cooking in RDS. Those of you who are familiar with Gas Station Simulator know precisely how the whole game is constructed. Since the beginning of the Road Diner Simulator production we’ve carefully analyzed your feedback and suggestions and we want to achieve something similar, yet take it to the next level. 

So, let me give you an example: Let’s say you want to prepare a classic Road Diner breakfast – scrambled eggs with bacon or sausage. You can approach it slowly and gently, step-by-step, ingredient by ingredient, but this costs time. Obviously, we won’t forbid you from running your own cozy diner with not much noise. 

However, if you’re looking for a challenge or for new ways to earn money quickly, that’s also possible. Each mini game gives you an opportunity to risk more. For instance: You can do multiple things at a time risking burning the above mentioned scrambled eggs and instead make an omelet. 


That’s why sayings like “Never Give Up” or “Practice Makes Perfect” have their use in Road Diner Simulator as well. Obviously, there will be some ways to calm those impatient clients – to be honest not sure what kind of ways but maybe a free coffee top-up would do the trick? I would be delighted to say the least. 

[h2]Stay in the loop 📰[/h2]

And that’s it for today, future diner owners! I’m really curious to see your thoughts regarding cooking in the Road Diner Simulator. Let me know in the comments down below what you think about the whole system. Also, if some of you have any suggestions to the game, don’t hesitate to leave your answers below as well. 

Now, I wanna know what would you like to see next? I already have in mind what I would like to show, but if there is anything that you’re curious about, fire it away in the comments. I’m gonna make sure to keep you guys updated on a regular basis from now on, so you can expect another announcement from me by the end of next month (definitely before Christmas tho). Until the next devlog! 

[i]P.S Our friends at Biotech Gameworks have just made available the long-awaited update to Kebab Chefs! - Restaurant Simulator, so I thought it was worth sharing this information with you. [/i]

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1001270/Kebab_Chefs__Restaurant_Simulator/

~Sewek

Apart from that, I’d like to do my best to share some more information about the whole universe and how Road Diner Sim and Gas Station Sim might work and interact with each other. In Road Diner Simulator, you're tasked with transforming a run-down diner into a bustling roadside eatery. From flipping burgers to managing staff, your skills will be put to the test as you strive to create the perfect dining experience for travelers and truckers alike. Whether you’re a master chef or a total rookie in this field, there’s always something new to cook up, new challenges to overcome, or not typical ways to learn a thing or two.  

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41182526/3a61cfbdb865b8f05c355b8c7fdc2626aac64047.jpg[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41182526/f885efb6eac5b5914d41ee534e97ef51e6199464.jpg[/img]

Owning both games might unlock unique items, events, and gameplay mechanics that you don’t want to miss. Imagine coordinating promotions between your gas station and diner to boost sales or dealing with a supply chain challenge that affects both operations! Okay... That might be too much and I might have my head in the clouds but hey – nobody can stop me from dreaming, right? 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41182526/66f753e9fc1acc1bcf52ba8245e5e4ad460d4437.jpg[/img]

The stage is yours right now, folks! Don’t hesitate to write your comments down below. While you eagerly wait for the next update, make sure to wishlist the game, so you avoid the fear of missing out on some fresh content. Until the next devlog! 👋

notes.title: Food in Road Diner
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41182526/b1a82b23a2408eb45cea1b93864da74de97ca3f2.jpg[/img]

Food is a crucial part of running a diner. With Road Diner, we want the game to be about running a diner rather than turning it into a cooking game. So a sort of balance has to be maintained and we believe we came up with a nice approach.

We are going to grab the cooking mechanics from our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1160920/Food_Truck_Simulator/]Food Truck Simulator[/url] and expand it to fit the needs of the Road Diner and later on Motel Simulator. However, in both cases we don’t want you to spend half the day in the kitchen making dishes. Instead, we want dedicated NPCs to handle the job. 

So why a cooking mechanics in the first place? Two reasons for that. First, we want you to give you the option to cook yourself in the early stages of the game to save some cash. Second, whatever dish you create to offer in your diner (and later motel), you will actually have to teach an employee how to prepare said dish with a real, hands-on approach so once he/she learns it, it will make this dish on their own in the future.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1149620/Gas_Station_Simulator/
If you also have a gas station in Gas Station Simulator built up, you will be able to offer some of the dishes that don’t spoil too quickly like sandwiches on the gas station as well. This provides benefits to the gas station and some extra income at the diner. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1792100/Motel_Simulator/
In Motel Simulator we will go with a very similar approach to food as again, that game is about running a motel rather than being a cook. The things that makes the Motel different from a diner when it comes to food are the customers and special requests they might have. What is however more important from the point of view of someone playing Road Diner is that a properly expanded diner will be able to cover the early culinary needs of the motel allowing you to focus on different areas first if you choose to do so.

notes.title: Customers have a story to tell…
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41182526/b1a82b23a2408eb45cea1b93864da74de97ca3f2.jpg[/img]

Customers are pretty much the backbone of running your business at the diner. If you are familiar with our customers in Gas Station Simulator, you might have noticed that we will need a lot more depth when it comes to customers for a diner since their stay at a diner is seldom as brief as it is on a gas station.

We hence decided to create a new customer system that all of our interconnected games will share. One key aspect of this new system is to give more depth to customers to have their unique personalities, interests and stories to tell on top of the stats and skills we need for Road Diner. Depending on how satisfied they are and how much time they spend at your business, the more they will open up. 

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1149620/Gas_Station_Simulator/

So when at the gas station, they will start dropping hints here and there, small remarks or let you in about their goals and/or journey, while spending more time at the road diner they will open up a lot more, especially if you already met them before while running the gas station. You will get to know them a lot better as they will be repeat customers.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1792100/Motel_Simulator/

In Motel Simulator, since their stay will be even longer, we will create events around those customers. So over the course of 2 or 3 games you get to know some of them pretty well and form a deeper relationship, especially since they will revisit your business - unless you do a really poor job running it and they will just stay away from your establishment. 

So in all 3 games we can look forward to a lot of happening when it comes to customers. We also want to create special customers who are from around the area and as you progress within the games will visit you more frequently providing more insights into your businesses and voicing their ideas for improvements or concerns more clearly and detailed than usual customers do. Like giving you a bit more of a helping hand.

notes.title: Dennis will be here!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41182526/08b4cfcd9b79037d4c16f9fade2aa79ab4efdd09.jpg[/img]

The love/hate relationship with Dennis will continue in Road Diner Simulator. Dennis, by players in Gas Station Simulator often referred to as "Dennis the Menace" will continue his mischief at the road diner. 
It makes perfect sense, since the diner is just across the street. 
He will not only continue to paint stupid things on your walls, but also break things and annoy your customers. 

Sure, you will be able to throw things at him to get him to leave, at least for a while, but there will also be new tools to deal with him at your disposal. For example, you will be able to call the local sheriff on him which will get rid of Dennis for a more extended period of time and comes with some interesting interactions when done multiple times.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1149620/Gas_Station_Simulator/

Another new way Dennis found to make your life just a little bit worse is to come up with the bright idea to open a lemonade stand at your diner stealing some of your customers. As you can imagine, early on when you are struggling to establish your diner this isn't really helping things. But here is where things get really interesting. Sure, you can deal with Dennis the usual way trying to get rid of him as you would expect, but you can try another approach: be nice!

Yeah right… being nice to Dennis?!? It’s an option with some interesting outcomes. One of those is eventually befriending Dennis and have him help you rather than annoy you. Now isn’t that something!

There is more Dennis related stuff being worked on in Road Diner Simulator, special interactions between [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1149620/Gas_Station_Simulator/]Gas Station Simulator[/url] and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1792100/Motel_Simulator/]Motel Simulator[/url] when it comes to Dennis and a whole new set of opportunities we will fore sure write more about in the future. We just figured you might be interested that Dennis is still going to play a role.

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1792100/Motel_Simulator/

notes.title: Trucks & Truckers
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41182526/5d9b85ccfff39045bc6d67e310b30636cb243e9b.jpg[/img]

More customer variety is a common request for Gas Station Simulator and something we are keeping in mind. We already have plans for bikers in the future and now adding another customer group that is missing just got a lot easier for us: truckers.

Massive long haul trucks is just what we need. And the truckers themselves are always an interesting bunch. We initially wanted to have trucks on the gas station with special fuel pumps and dedicated parking spaces, but we ran into some serious problems with the system handling the traffic. It is something we created early on, but then made the mistake to add and add tweaks onto it. At some point later in the game’s development we realised that the way we set it up and then expanded it simply won’t handle large trucks properly - or anything that “bends” somewhere like trailers etc.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35762680/03bc14c85faddbb702403cfe1526052e27d609ce.jpg[/img]

That is a mistake we didn’t make when creating the traffic system in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1160920/Food_Truck_Simulator/]Food Truck Simulator[/url]. While we used the Gas Station Simulator traffic system as a starting point there, we went into a different direction with it. And while there are no large trucks in Food Truck Simulator (yet), its traffic system already supports them. So since we are on a roll of [url=https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1149620/view/3363644258063773265]stealing stuff[/url] from them, we will do it again. It will require some more work to make it play nicely in Gas Station Simulator, but we don’t really have a choice in the long run:

https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/1792100/view/3359142561385503351

Yes, trucks and truckers are going to play a more significant role in Motel Simulator and since Motel Simulator, [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1747470/Road_Diner_Simulator/]Road Diner Simulator[/url] and Gas Station Simulator will have mechanics supporting each other, some of the content from one of the games will inevitably have to spill over to the others. In this case having a nice gas station here will provide incentives to truckers as customers for the motel and thus they will have to show up on the gas station. That is going to be so cool! This whole “making these games work together” approach is something that we are really excited about. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35762680/408bd7f90c68a5ed4036df32ff6dda992e75fc27.jpg[/img]

Just a reminder, Food Truck Simulator is going to be available on September, 14th. There is an updated demo, so you have a look at the traffic system there. It's a tad more sophisticated, no question about it:

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1149620/Gas_Station_Simulator/

notes.title: DevLog #1: Gas Station & Co
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41182526/38da3cdcf7aad749c76396db23799d6225a1e20f.jpg[/img]

Things are starting to happen a lot quicker in Road Diner Simulator now. 
With our workloads on [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1160920/Food_Truck_Simulator/]Food Truck Simulator[/url] slowing down and entering Early Access with [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1394960/Winter_Survival/]Winter Survival[/url] just around the corner, more of our focus is shifting towards Road Diner Simulator.

While being worked on more occasionally so far, recent the development started in earnest and will increase in pace over the next months. There is a lot of prototyping that is being done and many of the initial concepts being fleshed out in more detail and sometimes significantly changed or expanded during this process.

One of those things is how Road Diner Simulator will work and interact with our [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1149620/Gas_Station_Simulator/]Gas Station Simulator[/url] and later on with [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1792100/Motel_Simulator/]Motel Simulator[/url]. 

The idea behind Road Diner Simulator and in the same degree also behind Motel Simulator, is that those games are not only set in the game world and setting created by Gas Station Simulator, but actually all work together. They are separate games, but separate games that communicate with each other.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41182526/26b60cc4e2c6447f3e8398db1fc6c0b85f4cd7fd.jpg[/img]

As it’s evident by the picture above, the road diner is located just across the highway from the gas station. The first step of these games working together is to reflect the progress the player made in each game in the other two games. So in Gas Station Simulator you will see your diner exactly as you have build it in Road Diner Simulator and in there you will see your gas station the same way. And again, same applies to Motel Simulator. 

Each game will feature a special type of save file that the other games can access and read the state of your gas station, diner and motel from there. 

Showing the progress of the buildings in the other games is just the start, though. While it makes for neat visuals and creates a certain sense of accomplishment, there is a lot more to the connection between the games. And that comes in form of shared resources and various boosts across all games. 

A very simple example is the level. A gas station at level 5 will drive a lot more additional customers to the diner than a gas station that is just at its first level. For the motel and diner, the type of customer play a more significant role than it does in Gas Station Simulator. So the expansion of the diner will influence the customer type for the motel and vice-versa. For the progress of both to also be reflected on the gas station, Gas Station Simulator will see some new customers and new content with the release of both these games on top of what else we are doing there. 

Another area where these games play nice with each other is sharing various resources. Have a fully fledged out gas station making a nice revenue does not only influence various stats of your diner or motel, but allows you to channel some of its resources toward the new venture making the start just a bit easier. What’s more important however is being able later on to move some resources in either direction to deal with shortcoming on speed up the access to some of the advancements.  

Then there are direct boosts to various mechanics and mini-games that you perform within each of the games that work toward a common goal, but that’s something for a later DevLog.

As you can see, Gas Station Simulator, Road Diner Simulator and Motel Simulator, while separate games, will be able to benefit from your progress if you own and played any of the other games. You don’t have to, but we feel it makes a lot of sense to create interactions between games set in the same “universe”. And there are quite a few ideas in that area that we are toying with right now that will bring it even a step further. But more about those at a later point when final decisions are made.

notes.title: Announcing Gas Station Simulator’s first DLC
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41182526/edd5d7aa0d81b860027b43786479d24c6e6bb970.jpg[/img]

A lot is happening in and around Gas Station Simulator. With the announcements of Road Diner Simulator and recently Motel Simulator, we set the wheels in motion for new games set in the Gas Station “universe”. 

Things are happening for Gas Station Simulator itself as well. Today we are announcing the first DLC for the Gas Station Simulator: Can Touch This. This DLC will introduce far reaching customization options for your gas station, workshop and warehouse.

From customizing walls and roofs up to changing position of windows, doors, trashcans or cash register, the DLC offers many new things that might catch your eye.
Stickers that you can spray anywhere on your gas station, more interior & exterior decorations and also more levels and employees!

Can Touch This is coming on 11th of May 2022 and will be priced at $2,99! Add it to your wishlist now: 
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1940030/Gas_Station_Simulator__Can_Touch_This_DLC/?beta=0

notes.title: Announcing Motel Simulator
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41182526/57bde3bcf6ca4081d4563c34b81e7ead53ef1217.jpg[/img]

Road Diner will add a diner to the world of Gas Station Simulator and today we are announcing Motel Simulator will add a classic American motel there. 
Just like Road Diner, Motel Simulator will be very tightly integrated with both games and things you do on the gas station and/or at the diner, will influence the motel and vice-versa. 

Have a look at Motel Simulator’s store page and see what we plan to create. Add it to your wishlist if you like what you see:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1792100/Motel_Simulator/

There will be even more coming for Gas Station Simulator. Within the next 2 weeks we will announce the first 2 DLCs for the game, so stay tuned.
